en: to make them man and wife

examples.ko: 부모님은 딸을 일찍 결혼시키고 싶어 했어요.
examples.en: My parents wanted to marry their daughter off early.
Grandma got her eldest grandson married this spring.
After marrying off their son, the house became quiet.

examples.ko: 두 아이를 한꺼번에 결혼시키려면 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Marrying off two children at once costs a lot of money.

examples.ko: 저희 부모님은 내년에 누나를 결혼시킬 거예요.
examples.en: My parents are going to marry off my older sister next year.

examples.ko: 자식을 결혼시키는 일은 부모에게 큰 행사예요.
examples.en: Marrying off a child is a big event for parents.

explain: 주어는 보통 부모나 할머니처럼 결혼을 챙기는 어른이에요. '결혼하다'는 본인이 결혼하는 것이고, '결혼시키다'는 어른이 자식을 결혼하게 만드는 것이에요. 딸은 '시집보내다', 아들은 '장가보내다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: The subject is usually an adult who handles the wedding, like a parent or grandmother. '결혼하다' is the person marrying; '결혼시키다' is an adult getting a child married. For a daughter you can also say '시집보내다', and for a son '장가보내다'.

examples.en: I accidentally broke a cup while washing dishes.
The child almost broke the window with a ball.
If you're not careful, you'll break the plate.

examples.ko: 그 말이 조용한 분위기를 깨트리고 말았어요.
examples.en: Those words ended up breaking the quiet atmosphere.

examples.ko: 친구와 한 약속을 깨트리면 신뢰를 잃어요.
examples.en: If you break a promise to a friend, you lose trust.
Please crack the egg and put it in the frying pan.

explain: '깨뜨리다'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰이는 표준어예요. 스스로 깨지는 '깨지다'와 달리 누가 일부러나 실수로 깨는 일에 써요. 컵뿐 아니라 약속, 기록, 분위기를 깨는 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It is a standard word with the same meaning as '깨뜨리다'. Unlike '깨지다' (to break by itself), it is for someone breaking something on purpose or by accident. Besides cups, it is used figuratively for promises, records and moods.

examples.en: I watched a musical at the grand theater.
A grand theater has very many seats.

examples.ko: 오늘 공연은 대극장이 아니라 소극장에서 해요.
examples.en: Today's show is in the small theater, not the grand theater.
I decided to meet my friend in front of the grand theater.
It takes ten minutes on foot to the grand theater.

examples.ko: 저는 대극장보다 작은 극장이 더 좋아요.
examples.en: I like small theaters better than the grand theater.

explain: 극장 크기에 따라 대극장, 중극장, 소극장이라고 나눠 불러요. 소극장은 배우가 가까이 보이고 대극장은 무대가 크고 좌석이 많아요. 영화를 보는 곳은 보통 '영화관'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Theaters are divided by size into '대극장', '중극장' and '소극장'. In a '소극장' the actors seem close, while a '대극장' has a big stage and many seats. A place to watch movies is usually called a '영화관'.

examples.ko: 밤사이 날씨가 악화되면서 비가 더 세졌어요.
examples.en: The weather got worse overnight and the rain grew heavier.

examples.ko: 밤사이 폭설이 내려서 아침에 차가 눈에 파묻혀 있었어요.
examples.en: Heavy snow fell overnight, so in the morning the car was buried in snow.
The flowers in the pot bloomed fully overnight.

examples.ko: 밤사이 문자가 열 통이나 와 있었어요.
examples.en: Ten text messages had come in overnight.

examples.ko: 밤사이의 기온 차가 커서 감기 걸리기 쉬워요.
examples.en: The temperature difference during the night is big, so it's easy to catch a cold.

examples.ko: 밤사이 누가 다녀갔는지 문 앞에 택배가 있어요.
examples.en: Someone must have come by overnight, since there's a package at the door.

explain: '밤새'는 '밤사이'를 줄인 말이라 같은 뜻으로 써요. 다만 '밤새 울었어요'처럼 '밤새'는 밤 내내 계속된 일에도 많이 써요. '밤사이'는 자는 동안 어느새 변한 일을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '밤새' is a shortened form of '밤사이', so they can mean the same. But '밤새' is also used for something that lasted all night, as in '밤새 울었어요'. '밤사이' fits well when something changed while you were asleep.

examples.en: Hearing your voice puts me at ease.
I felt relieved when I heard the child got home.
I felt relieved because the doctor said it's fine.

examples.ko: 옆에 친구가 있으면 안심돼서 잠이 와요.
examples.en: With a friend beside me I feel safe and get sleepy.
Hearing the rain has stopped, I feel a bit relieved.
I'm waiting for some reassuring news.

explain: '안심하다'는 내가 마음을 놓는 행동이고, '안심되다'는 어떤 일 때문에 저절로 마음이 놓이는 느낌이에요. 보통 '~니까/~어서 안심돼요'처럼 이유와 같이 말해요. 반대는 '불안하다'예요.
explain_en: '안심하다' is the act of putting your mind at rest, while '안심되다' is the feeling of being put at ease by something. It usually comes with a reason, as in '~니까/~어서 안심돼요'. The opposite is '불안하다'.

examples.en: For safety, hold the steering wheel with both hands.

examples.ko: 이 차는 운전대가 너무 무거워서 힘들어요.
examples.en: The steering wheel of this car is too heavy, so it is hard.
On cold winter mornings the steering wheel is cold.
My father is holding the steering wheel right now.

examples.ko: 주차할 때는 운전대를 천천히 돌려 보세요.
examples.en: When you park, try turning the steering wheel slowly.
Do not take the wheel when you are sleepy.

explain: 일상에서는 '핸들'이라고 더 자주 말해요. 영어 handle에서 온 말인데, 영어의 handle은 손잡이라서 자동차 운전대는 steering wheel이라고 해요. 그래서 영어를 쓰는 사람에게 '핸들'이라고 하면 못 알아들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: In daily speech Koreans say '핸들' more often. It comes from the English word handle, but in English a handle is a grip, and the car part is called a steering wheel. So an English speaker may not understand Korean '핸들'.

examples.ko: 그 배우가 카메라를 보고 윙크를 했어요.
examples.en: The actor winked at the camera.
My friend smiled and greeted me with a wink.

examples.ko: 아기가 윙크가 안 돼서 두 눈을 다 감았어요.
examples.en: The baby couldn't wink and closed both eyes.
My face turned red at his wink.

examples.ko: 사진을 찍을 때 윙크도 해 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried winking too when taking the photo.
One wink eased the mood.

explain: '윙크를 하다'가 기본이고 '윙크하다'로 붙여 써도 돼요. 한쪽 눈만 감는 동작이라서, 두 눈을 다 깜빡이는 '눈을 깜빡이다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: The basic form is 윙크를 하다, and 윙크하다 is also fine. It means closing only one eye, so it differs from blinking both eyes (눈을 깜빡이다).

examples.ko: 어제 못 본 드라마를 재방송으로 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the drama I missed yesterday as a re-run.
This program is re-aired on weekends.
The re-run comes on at ten in the morning.
Even just watching the re-run, I can understand the whole story.

examples.ko: 인기 있는 드라마는 재방송도 자주 해요.
examples.en: Popular dramas are re-aired often too.

examples.ko: 저는 재방송에서 처음 그 가수를 봤어요.
examples.en: I first saw that singer in a re-run.

explain: 처음 방송하는 것은 '본방송', 줄여서 '본방'이라고 해요. 본방을 놓친 드라마는 재방송으로 보면 돼요.
explain_en: The first airing is called 본방송, shortened to 본방. If you miss a drama on its first airing, you can watch the 재방송 instead.

examples.en: In winter I sleep with the electric mat on.
If the electric mat is too hot, lower the temperature.

examples.ko: 전기장판 위에 누우면 몸이 사르르 풀려요.
examples.en: When I lie on the electric mat, my body relaxes.

examples.ko: 할머니 방에 새 전기장판을 깔아 드렸어요.
examples.en: I laid a new electric mat in Grandmother's room.
It's dangerous to leave an electric mat on for a long time.
Thanks to the electric mat, I run the boiler less.

explain: '전기요'라고도 해요. '켜다/끄다', '깔다'와 함께 써요. 오래 켜 두고 자면 저온 화상을 입을 수 있어서 조심하라는 말을 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It is also called '전기요'. It goes with '켜다/끄다' (turn on/off) and '깔다' (lay out). You often hear warnings to be careful, since sleeping on it for long can cause low-temperature burns.

examples.en: That actor was cast as the lead.
I did the audition, was cast in the drama, and was happy.

examples.ko: 캐스팅된 배우들이 첫 대본 리딩을 했어요.
examples.en: The actors who were cast did their first script reading.
She was scouted on the street and became a model.

examples.ko: 제가 캐스팅될 거라고는 생각도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I never imagined I would be cast.
I am curious about how people get cast in movies.

explain: 능동은 '캐스팅하다', 피동은 '캐스팅되다'예요. 역할 이름에는 '주인공으로'처럼 '으로'를 붙여요. 영어 cast에서 온 말이라 줄여서 명사 '캐스팅'으로도 써요.
explain_en: The active form is '캐스팅하다' and this is the passive. The role takes '으로', as in '주인공으로 캐스팅되다' (be cast as the lead). It comes from English 'cast', and the noun '캐스팅' is also used.

en: to become white; to turn white

examples.ko: 눈이 내려서 온 동네가 하얘지는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the whole neighborhood turn white as the snow fell.

examples.ko: 긴장하면 머릿속이 하얘지고 아무 말도 안 나와요.
examples.en: When I get nervous, my mind goes blank and I can't say anything.
Does your skin get whiter if you apply this cream?

examples.ko: 머리카락이 하얘지기 시작해서 염색을 할까 고민이에요.
examples.en: My hair is starting to turn white, so I am thinking about dyeing it.

examples.ko: 표백제를 쓰면 하얘지긴 하지만 옷감이 상해요.
examples.en: Bleach does make clothes whiter, but it damages the fabric.
I endured it even though the pain made my face go pale.

explain: '하얗다'가 ㅎ 불규칙이라 '하얘요, 하얘졌어요'처럼 모양이 바뀌어요. 눈, 머리카락처럼 색이 변할 때뿐 아니라 놀라거나 아파서 얼굴이 창백해질 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 면접에서 질문을 듣는 순간 머릿속이 하얘졌어요.
phrases.en: The moment I heard the question in the interview, my mind went blank.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라거나 긴장해서 아무 생각도 나지 않는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state where you are so startled or nervous that no thoughts come to mind.

explain_en: '하얗다' is an ㅎ-irregular verb, so the form changes as in '하얘요' and '하얘졌어요'. It is used not only for color changes like snow or hair, but also when your face goes pale from shock or pain.
